title: Full-back overlaps: come inside
brief: Your #8 has the ball facing forward, and your full-back sprints up the touchline past you.
briefKid: Your midfielder has the ball. Your defender sprints up the sideline, past you.
question: Your full-back now holds the width. Where do you go?
questionKid: Your defender is out wide now. Where do you go?

takeaway.standard: The full-back and winger never share the touchline: when the full-back overlaps, you come inside into the half-space between their lines, which drags their full-back inside and frees yours.
takeaway.kid: Teammate runs past you on the outside? Move inside into your own lane.

notes: Authored answer (engine disagreement). Layer A ignores tags.widthHolders and the overridden full-back, so the winger's base stays on the touchline beside the overlapping full-back: base (70.7, 64.0). In engine mode the ghost is (71.7, 60.0), still in the wing lane 5 m from the full-back, and the start spot (70, 64), 2 m from him, scores 90 (S). B6 says the winger comes inside when the full-back overlaps, so the zone is centred on the half-space pocket between their full-back and centre-back, in front of their back line; the rules agree there (ghost 98: lane-open, occupancy, support-distance and offside 1.00, between-lines 0.78 because their lines are only 4.7 m apart).

misconceptions.text: You stayed on the touchline with your full-back, so one defender can mark you both and the overlap is wasted.
misconceptions.textKid: You and your defender are in the same lane. Move inside.

misconceptions.text: You came all the way into the middle next to your #9, so their centre-back can mark you both; stop in the channel between their full-back and centre-back.
misconceptions.textKid: Too far inside. Stop in the gap between their defenders.
